agent.howItWorksBody: The {{name}} agent is a small daemon that runs on the host and forwards local events to UTMStack over an authenticated TLS connection. It auto-updates and reports its health.
agent.installHint: Run this command on every {{name}} host you want to monitor. The token already encodes your current workspace.
agent.after1: The host appears under Data Sources within ~60 seconds of agent start.
agent.after2: Telemetry begins flowing into Log Explorer, scoped to your workspace.
agent.after3: The agent self-reports CPU / memory / disk health back to UTMStack.

collector.howItWorksBody: {{name}} doesn't run a UTMStack agent. Instead, you install the UTMStack collector somewhere on the network that both your {{name}} device and UTMStack can reach. {{name}} sends syslog to the collector, the collector parses, normalizes, and forwards events into UTMStack.
collector.step1Hint: Run on a Linux host with network access from the {{name}} device.
collector.step2Hint: On the {{name}} device, point syslog forwarding to the collector's address on {{port}}.
collector.step3Body: Within a few minutes you should see {{name}} events under source: {{source}} in Log Explorer, and a new entry in Data Sources.

endpoint.title: Where to send {{name}} events
endpoint.hint: Point {{name}} at the UTMStack collector listener using the values below.

sendLogs.title: 1 · Send logs to UTMStack
sendLogs.body: Configure your device to send syslog messages over UDP (514) or TCP (514) to the UTMStack agent.

enableCollector.title: 2 · Enable the syslog collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the syslog integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so events start flowing into Log Explorer.

sendLogs.title: 1 · Send NetFlow to UTMStack
sendLogs.body: Configure your device to send NetFlow records to the UTMStack agent on port 2055/UDP.

enableCollector.title: 2 · Enable the NetFlow collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the NetFlow integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so NetFlow records start flowing.

sendLogs.title: 1 · Send logs to UTMStack
sendLogs.body: Configure your Cisco device to forward syslog to the UTMStack agent (UDP 514 or TCP 514).

enableCollector.title: 2 · Enable the Cisco collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the Cisco integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Cisco events start flowing.

sendLogs.title: 1 · Configure ESXi to forward syslog
sendLogs.body: On each ESXi host, set Syslog.global.logHost to point at the UTMStack agent (e.g. tcp://<collector>:514) and open the syslog firewall ruleset.

enableCollector.title: 2 · Enable the VMware collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the VMware integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so ESXi events start flowing.

requirements.title: 1 · Requirements
requirements.body: Ensure the AS/400 (IBM i) can reach the UTMStack collector and that QAUDJRN journaling is enabled.

installCollector.title: 2 · Install the log collector
installCollector.body: Install the UTMStack collector on a host that can reach the AS/400 and configure the AS/400 module.

configure.title: 3 · Configure the AS/400 integration
configure.body: Provide the AS/400 host, credentials, and journal name in the collector's configuration file.

activate.title: 4 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so AS/400 events start flowing.

myAccount.title: 1 · Open My Account
myAccount.body: In the Bitdefender GravityZone console, click on "My Account".

accessUrl.title: 2 · Note the Access URL
accessUrl.body: Scroll down to the Control Center API section and save the Access URL — you'll need it in later steps. Then open the API key section and click Add at the top of the table.

createApiKey.title: 3 · Create an API key
createApiKey.body: Write a description for the API key and select the Event Push Service API option. Click Save.

licensing.title: 5 · Note the Company IDs
licensing.body: Open the Licensing section and save the Company IDs you want to monitor.

addInstances.title: 6 · Add your GravityZone instances
addInstances.body: Add the Bitdefender GravityZone instances using the Access URL, API key, and Company IDs you collected.

activate.title: 7 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Bitdefender events start flowing.

openMenu.title: 1 · Open the More menu
openMenu.body: In the ESET Protect sidebar, click on the "More" menu.

serverConfig.title: 2 · Server configuration
serverConfig.body: Click on the "Server configuration" submenu in the ESET Protect sidebar.

advancedSettings.title: 3 · Advanced settings
advancedSettings.body: Click on "Advanced settings" to expand the list of configurations.

syslogServer.title: 4 · Configure Syslog server
syslogServer.body: Scroll down to "Syslog server", enable "Export logs to Syslog", and point it at the UTMStack agent on 514/udp or 514/tcp.

enableCollector.title: 5 · Enable the ESET collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the ESET integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 6 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so ESET events start flowing.

consoleSettings.title: 1 · Open Console Settings
consoleSettings.body: In the Kaspersky Security sidebar, click "Console Settings" → "Integration".

siem.title: 2 · Open the SIEM integration
siem.body: Within Integration, open the SIEM section and click on the "Settings" link.

configure.title: 3 · Configure Splunk(CEF) forwarding
configure.body: Configure Kaspersky Security to send logs in Splunk(CEF) format to the UTMStack agent on 514/udp or 514/tcp.

enableCollector.title: 4 · Enable the Kaspersky collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the Kaspersky integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 5 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Kaspersky events start flowing.

createApiCredentials.title: 1 · Create API credentials
createApiCredentials.body: In Sophos Central, go to Global Settings → API Credentials and create a new API credential with read access.

tenantId.title: 2 · Note your tenant ID
tenantId.body: Open the credential and copy the Client ID, Client Secret, and tenant ID — you'll paste them into the form below.

fillForm.title: 3 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the credential values to UTMStack.

activate.title: 4 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Sophos events start flowing.

login.title: 1 · Log in to the management console
login.body: Log in to the Webroot management console. It opens on the Sites tab.

apiAccess.title: 3 · Open API Access
apiAccess.body: From the Subscriptions tab, click on the API Access tab.

createCredential.title: 4 · Create a client credential
createCredential.body: Click New and fill in the Name and Description. Read the SecureAnywhere Business Solution and Unity API agreement, then click Create.

noteClientSecret.title: 5 · Copy the client ID and secret
noteClientSecret.body: Save the Client ID from the list and the Client Secret that's shown only once. Click "I have made note of the client secret" to confirm.

fillForm.title: 6 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the client ID and client secret to UTMStack. You can add more than one Webroot tenant if needed.

activate.title: 7 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Webroot events start flowing.

createApiToken.title: 1 · Create an API token
createApiToken.body: In SentinelOne, go to Settings → Users → Create User of type Service User and generate an API token with read access.

consoleUrl.title: 2 · Note your console URL
consoleUrl.body: Copy the console URL (e.g. https://my-org.sentinelone.net) — UTMStack uses it to call the API.

fillForm.title: 3 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the console URL and API token to UTMStack.

activate.title: 4 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so SentinelOne events start flowing.

createApiClient.title: 1 · Create an API client
createApiClient.body: In CrowdStrike Falcon, go to Support → API Clients and Keys, and create a new API client.

setScopes.title: 2 · Grant the required scopes
setScopes.body: Grant read access to the events and detections scopes you want UTMStack to ingest.

copyCredentials.title: 3 · Copy the credentials
copyCredentials.body: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret — the secret is shown only once.

fillForm.title: 4 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the credentials and the CrowdStrike cloud region to UTMStack.

activate.title: 5 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so CrowdStrike events start flowing.

azurePortal.title: 1 · Open the Azure Portal
azurePortal.body: Open the Azure Portal and click on Microsoft Entra ID.

registerApp.title: 3 · Register a new app
registerApp.body: Click "New registration" and fill the form: name it "UTMStack O365 Agent" and select "Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single-tenant)". Click Register.

clientSecret.title: 4 · Create a client secret
clientSecret.body: In the new App registration, go to Certificates & Secrets → New client secret. Add a description, set expiry to 730 days, and click Add. Copy the value somewhere safe.

apiPermissions.title: 5 · Add Office 365 Management API permissions
apiPermissions.body: Open API Permissions → Add Permissions → look for "Office 365 Management API".

activityFeed.title: 6 · Grant Application permissions
activityFeed.body: Select "Application Permissions" and add ActivityFeed.Read and ActivityFeed.ReadDlp. Click "Grant admin consent" and confirm.

graphPermissions.title: 7 · Add Microsoft Graph permissions
graphPermissions.body: From the "Request API Permissions" dialog, click "Microsoft Graph".

delegatedPermissions.title: 8 · Add delegated SecurityAlert permissions
delegatedPermissions.body: Select "Delegated Permissions" and add SecurityAlert.Read.All and SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All. Click "Grant admin consent" and confirm.

appPermissions.title: 9 · Add application SecurityAlert permissions
appPermissions.body: Select "Application Permissions" and add SecurityAlert.Read.All and SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All. Click "Grant admin consent" and confirm.

noteIds.title: 10 · Note the IDs
noteIds.body: Go to the Overview section of the App registration and copy the Client ID, Tenant ID, and the secret value.

fillForm.title: 11 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the values to UTMStack. You can add more than one Office 365 tenant.

activate.title: 12 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Office 365 events start flowing.

openSettings.title: 1 · Open repository/organization settings
openSettings.body: Open the Settings page of your GitHub repository or organization.

addWebhook.title: 2 · Add the webhook
addWebhook.body: Click Webhooks → Add webhook. Point the Payload URL at the UTMStack ingestion endpoint, set Content type to application/json, and set a secret you'll paste into UTMStack as well.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so GitHub events start flowing.

openSetup.title: 1 · Open Setup
openSetup.body: Go to Setup and select "Setup for the current app" at the top right of the screen.

appManager.title: 2 · Open App Manager
appManager.body: Type "App Manager" in the quick search box and select App Manager.

newConnectedApp.title: 3 · Create a new Connected App
newConnectedApp.body: On the Lightning Experience App Manager screen, click "New Connected App" and fill in the fields.

oauthSettings.title: 4 · Enable OAuth Settings
oauthSettings.body: In the "API (Enable OAuth Settings)" section, check "Enable OAuth Settings" and use https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/success as the Callback URL.

oauthScopes.title: 5 · Add OAuth scopes
oauthScopes.body: Select "Access Connect REST API resources (chatter_api)" under Selected OAuth Scopes.

save.title: 6 · Save
save.body: Save your changes and select Continue on the next screen.

manageConsumer.title: 7 · Open Manage Consumer Details
manageConsumer.body: Inside your Connected App, go to "API (Enable OAuth Settings)" and click "Manage Consumer Details" next to Consumer Key and Secret.

copyCredentials.title: 8 · Copy the consumer key and secret
copyCredentials.body: Verify your identity. The Consumer Key and Consumer Secret appear under "Consumer Details". Copy both with the Copy button.

fillForm.title: 9 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the Consumer Key, Consumer Secret, Salesforce username and password to UTMStack.

activate.title: 10 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Salesforce events start flowing.

enableModule.title: 1 · Enable the IIS Filebeat module
enableModule.body:
On the UTMStack agent host, run:
cd "C:\Program Files\UTMStack\UTMStack Agent\beats\filebeat\" && filebeat modules enable iis

configureModule.title: 2 · Configure the IIS module
configureModule.body: Edit C:\Program Files\UTMStack\UTMStack Agent\beats\filebeat\modules.d\iis.yml as shown below to point at the IIS log directories you want to ship.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so IIS events start flowing.

installRsyslog.title: 1 · Install rsyslog
installRsyslog.body: Ensure rsyslog is installed on the host. Use your distribution's package manager (apt, dnf, yum).

configureRsyslog.title: 2 · Configure rsyslog to forward to UTMStack
configureRsyslog.body: Edit /etc/rsyslog.conf (or a file under /etc/rsyslog.d/) and add a forwarding rule that targets the UTMStack agent over UDP or TCP on port 514.

restartRsyslog.title: 3 · Restart rsyslog
restartRsyslog.body: Restart the rsyslog service: sudo systemctl restart rsyslog

enableCollector.title: 4 · Enable the Linux logs collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the Linux Logs integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

overview.title: 1 · Use the HTTP/JSON ingestion endpoint
overview.body: UTMStack accepts arbitrary JSON events over HTTPS. Send a POST request with a list of events; UTMStack parses them and routes through your configured parser.

auth.title: 2 · Authenticate with a federation token
auth.body: Get a federation token from Settings → Connection Key and send it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

endpoint.title: JSON ingestion endpoint
endpoint.hint: Use this request shape from your application or a cron job. The token is the federation key from Settings → Connection Key.

openServerManager.title: 1 · Open Server Manager
openServerManager.body: On the AD domain controller, open Server Manager.

addRoles.title: 2 · Add Roles and Features
addRoles.body: Choose "Add roles and features" from the Manage menu.

selectCertServices.title: 3 · Select Active Directory Certificate Services
selectCertServices.body: On the Server Roles step, select Active Directory Certificate Services.

installServices.title: 4 · Install the Certificate Authority role service
installServices.body: On the Role Services step, select Certificate Authority and finish the wizard.

configureAdCs.title: 5 · Configure AD CS
configureAdCs.body: After install, click the notification to configure AD CS and choose Certificate Authority as the role service to configure.

pickCaType.title: 6 · Pick the CA type
pickCaType.body: Choose Enterprise CA → Root CA → Create a new private key.

setValidity.title: 7 · Set the certificate validity period
setValidity.body: Set a validity period that fits your organization (5 years is typical).

confirm.title: 8 · Confirm and install
confirm.body: Review the settings and click Configure to finish.

restart.title: 9 · Restart the domain controller
restart.body: Restart the domain controller so LDAPS becomes available on TCP 636.

activate.title: 10 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so AD audit events start flowing.

enableAudit.title: 1 · Enable auditing
enableAudit.body: On the Oracle Database instance, enable standard auditing or Unified Auditing depending on your version.

configureTrail.title: 2 · Configure the audit trail
configureTrail.body: Set audit_trail=OS or audit_trail=XML,EXTENDED so audit records are written to files Filebeat can collect.

exportTrail.title: 3 · Make audit files readable
exportTrail.body: Ensure the audit_file_dest directory is readable by the UTMStack agent's user.

enableCollector.title: 4 · Enable the Oracle collector
enableCollector.body: Enable the log collector and the Oracle integration in the configuration file where your UTMStack agent is installed.

activate.title: 5 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Oracle audit events start flowing.

overview.title: 1 · About the vulnerabilities scanner
overview.body: The UTMStack vulnerabilities module scans assets discovered through the Asset Management module and matches their fingerprint against the CVE database.

scope.title: 2 · Define scan scope
scope.body: Use the Asset Management module to register the hosts you want scanned. The vulnerabilities scanner will run periodically against them.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module to start scanning.

overview.title: 1 · About Asset Management
overview.body: The Asset Management module discovers and inventories hosts, software, and services across your network.

agentRequirement.title: 2 · Agent requirement
agentRequirement.body: Asset discovery uses UTMStack agents running on Linux, Windows, or macOS hosts. Install the agent on the systems you want inventoried.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module to start asset discovery.

enableAuditPolicy.title: 1 · Enable Audit Object Access
enableAuditPolicy.body: On the Windows host, open Group Policy → Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration → Object Access and enable "Audit File System".

configureFolderAuditing.title: 2 · Configure folder auditing
configureFolderAuditing.body: On each folder you want monitored, open Properties → Security → Advanced → Auditing and add an auditing entry for the principals and access types you care about.

verifyEvents.title: 3 · Verify events appear in Security log
verifyEvents.body: Open Event Viewer and confirm 4663/4670 events are being generated when the audited objects are accessed.

activate.title: 4 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so file integrity events start flowing.

overview.title: 1 · About SOC AI
overview.body: SOC AI augments UTMStack with an LLM-backed analyst that summarizes alerts and suggests next steps. It runs against the provider you configure.

chooseProvider.title: 2 · Choose a provider
chooseProvider.body: Pick a provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Ollama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Groq, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

configureCredentials.title: 3 · Configure credentials
configureCredentials.body: Provide the API key and (where applicable) the model name and endpoint URL.

activate.title: 4 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so SOC AI starts working on alerts.

requirements.title: 1 · Requirements
requirements.body: Self-monitoring runs on an UTMStack agent installed on the UTMStack host itself. Ubuntu and Red Hat-family distributions are supported.

installAgent.title: 2 · Install the agent
installAgent.body: Install the UTMStack agent on the UTMStack host using the architecture-specific installer.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so self-monitoring telemetry starts flowing.

enableAuditPolicy.title: 1 · Enable Audit Object Access
enableAuditPolicy.body: On the Windows host, open Group Policy → Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration → Object Access and enable "Audit File System".

configureFolderAuditing.title: 2 · Configure folder auditing
configureFolderAuditing.body: On each folder you want monitored, open Properties → Security → Advanced → Auditing and add an auditing entry for the principals and access types you care about.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so file activity events start flowing.

openConsole.title: 1 · Open the Elastic Beanstalk console
openConsole.body: In the AWS Console, open Elastic Beanstalk.

environment.title: 2 · Open the environment management page
environment.body: Navigate to the management page for the environment you want to monitor.

software.title: 4 · Modify the Software configuration
software.body: In the Software configuration category, choose Modify.

s3LogStorage.title: 5 · Enable S3 log storage
s3LogStorage.body: Under S3 log storage, choose Rotate logs to upload rotated logs to Amazon S3.

cloudwatchStreaming.title: 6 · Enable CloudWatch Logs streaming
cloudwatchStreaming.body: Under Instance log streaming to CloudWatch Logs, enable streaming, set the retention period, and pick whether to upload existing logs.

activate.title: 7 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Beanstalk events start flowing.

taskDefinition.title: 1 · Update your task definition
taskDefinition.body: In the task definition for the Fargate task, set the logDriver to "awslogs" and define the log group name.

cloudwatchLogs.title: 2 · Confirm CloudWatch Logs is receiving logs
cloudwatchLogs.body: Open the CloudWatch Logs console and confirm the log group is being populated when tasks run.

iamPrerequisite.title: 3 · IAM user prerequisite
iamPrerequisite.body: This integration shares credentials with the AWS IAM User module — make sure it's configured with CloudWatchLogsReadOnlyAccess.

activate.title: 4 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Fargate events start flowing.

iamConsole.title: 1 · Open the IAM console
iamConsole.body: In the AWS console, go to IAM → Users → Add users.

createUser.title: 2 · Create the user
createUser.body: Pick a username (e.g. utmstack-ingest). Choose programmatic access.

review.title: 5 · Review the user
review.body: Review the user details and click Create user.

copyKeys.title: 6 · Copy the access key ID and secret
copyKeys.body: Copy the Access key ID and the Secret access key — the secret is shown only once.

createLogGroup.title: 7 · Create a CloudWatch log group
createLogGroup.body: In CloudWatch → Log groups, create a log group named "utmstack" — other AWS integrations will deliver to it.

fillForm.title: 8 · Fill the form
fillForm.body: Provide the access key, secret, default region, and the log group name (e.g. "utmstack") to UTMStack.

activate.title: 9 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so AWS events start flowing.

iamPrerequisite.title: 1 · IAM user prerequisite
iamPrerequisite.body: Lambda relies on the AWS IAM User module — make sure that integration is configured first with CloudWatchLogsReadOnlyAccess.

cloudwatchStream.title: 2 · Lambda already streams to CloudWatch Logs
cloudwatchStream.body: AWS Lambda automatically publishes execution logs to CloudWatch Logs under /aws/lambda/<function_name>. UTMStack ingests from the log group you configured in the IAM user setup.

activate.title: 3 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so Lambda events start flowing.

pickDb.title: 2 · Pick the DB instance
pickDb.body: In the navigation pane, choose Databases and select the DB instance you want to monitor.

logExports.title: 4 · Enable Log Exports
logExports.body: In the Log exports section, choose Error log and Agent log to publish to CloudWatch Logs.

apply.title: 5 · Apply changes
apply.body: Choose Continue, then Modify DB Instance on the summary page.

activate.title: 6 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so SQL Server events start flowing.

pickDb.title: 2 · Pick the DB instance
pickDb.body: In the navigation pane, choose Databases and select the DB instance you want to modify.

logExports.title: 3 · Enable Log Exports
logExports.body: In the Log exports section, choose the PostgreSQL log to publish to CloudWatch Logs.

apply.title: 4 · Apply changes
apply.body: Choose Continue, then Modify DB Instance on the summary page.

activate.title: 5 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so PostgreSQL events start flowing.

createTarget.title: 1 · Create a traffic mirror target
createTarget.body: In the VPC console, create a Traffic Mirror Target that points at the network interface of the UTMStack agent VM.

createFilter.title: 2 · Create a traffic mirror filter
createFilter.body: Create a Traffic Mirror Filter and add inbound/outbound rules for the protocols you want to mirror (e.g. all TCP, all UDP).

createSession.title: 3 · Create a traffic mirror session
createSession.body: Create a Traffic Mirror Session that pairs each source network interface with the target and filter you created.

iamPrerequisite.title: 4 · IAM user prerequisite
iamPrerequisite.body: Make sure the AWS IAM User module is also configured so UTMStack can read VPC flow logs if needed.

activate.title: 5 · Activate
activate.body: Activate the UTMStack module so mirrored traffic starts being parsed.

cloud.howItWorksBody: {{name}} runs entirely inside UTMStack — no agent or collector to deploy. Provide read-only API credentials and UTMStack will pull events on a schedule, parse them, and ingest them into Log Explorer.
cloud.after1: UTMStack performs an initial backfill of recent events.
cloud.after2: From then on, events are pulled every 1–5 minutes (depends on the API).
cloud.after3: The integration appears under Data Sources with current pull status and lag.

tenants.title: Configured tenants
tenants.empty: No tenants configured yet. Add your first one below.
tenants.invalidJson: Could not parse the file as JSON.
tenants.createError: Could not create the tenant. Please try again.
tenants.updateError: Could not update the tenant. Please try again.

createTopic.title: 1 · Create a Pub/Sub topic
createTopic.body: In the Google Cloud console, open Pub/Sub → Topics and create a new topic. UTMStack will receive events through this topic.

createSubscription.title: 2 · Create a subscription
createSubscription.body: Inside the topic, create a Pull subscription. UTMStack pulls messages from this subscription.

configureSubscription.title: 3 · Configure the subscription
configureSubscription.body: Set the message retention duration to a value that fits your tolerance for downtime (default 7 days is fine). Leave acknowledgement deadline at 10 seconds and expiration to Never expire.

logsRouter.title: 4 · Open Logs Router
logsRouter.body: Navigate to Logging → Logs Router and create a new sink. This is what forwards your project's logs into the Pub/Sub topic above.

sinkDestination.title: 5 · Point the sink at the topic
sinkDestination.body: Choose Cloud Pub/Sub topic as the sink destination and select the topic you created. Use the inclusion/exclusion filters to scope what is forwarded.

serviceAccount.title: 6 · Create a service account
serviceAccount.body: Open IAM & Admin → Service Accounts and create a new service account. Grant it the Pub/Sub Editor role so UTMStack can pull from the subscription.

serviceAccountKey.title: 7 · Generate a key for the service account
serviceAccountKey.body: Open the service account, go to the Keys tab, and add a new key. Pick JSON as the key type.

downloadKey.title: 8 · Download and paste the JSON key
downloadKey.body: Save the JSON file Google downloads — its contents go in the Service account JSON field below.

eventHub.title: 1 · Create an Event Hub
eventHub.body: In the Azure Portal, create an Event Hubs namespace and an Event Hub inside it. UTMStack will read events from this hub.

sharedAccessPolicy.title: 2 · Add a Shared Access Policy
sharedAccessPolicy.body: Open the Event Hub → Shared access policies and create a new policy with the Listen permission only.

connectionString.title: 3 · Copy the primary connection string
connectionString.body: Open the policy and copy the Connection string–primary key. It looks like: Endpoint=sb://...;SharedAccessKeyName=...;SharedAccessKey=...

consumerGroup.title: 4 · Create a dedicated consumer group
consumerGroup.body: Open the Event Hub → Consumer groups and create a new one for UTMStack. Don't reuse $Default — give UTMStack its own group so checkpoints don't collide with other consumers.

storageAccount.title: 5 · Create a Storage Account
storageAccount.body: UTMStack needs a Storage Account for checkpointing. Create one in the same region as the Event Hub.

storageContainer.title: 6 · Create a container inside the Storage Account
storageContainer.body: Inside the Storage Account → Containers, create a new container. Note the container name and the Storage Account connection string (Access keys → Connection string).

eventGrid.title: 7 · Register the Event Grid resource provider
eventGrid.body: In Subscriptions → Resource providers, register Microsoft.EventGrid if it isn't already. This lets Azure forward subscription-level events to your Event Hub.

eventSubscription.title: 8 · Create an Event Subscription
eventSubscription.body: Create an Event Subscription that targets your Event Hub. Choose the event types you want to forward to UTMStack.

prerequisite.title: Prerequisite · IAM user
prerequisite.body: Before this integration can work, you need an IAM user for UTMStack with the CloudWatchLogsReadOnlyAccess policy. Capture its access key ID and secret access key — you'll paste them into the tenant form below.

createTrail.title: 1 · Create a trail
createTrail.body: In the CloudTrail panel, select "Create trail".

s3Buckets.title: 3 · Select S3 buckets
s3Buckets.body: Mark "Select all S3 buckets in your account".

bucketName.title: 4 · Create the S3 bucket
bucketName.body: Fill in the "S3 bucket" field. The bucket name must be unique across S3. Then click "Create".

editTrail.title: 5 · Open the trail to edit
editTrail.body: Click on the name of the trail to edit it.

cloudwatchConfig.title: 6 · Configure CloudWatch Logs
cloudwatchConfig.body: Open the CloudWatch Logs section and enable the integration so the trail forwards events to a log group.

logGroup.title: 7 · Set the log group name
logGroup.body: Fill the log group name (e.g. utmstack) and continue. Use this same name in the "Log group name" field below.

permissions.title: 8 · Grant CloudTrail permissions
permissions.body: Click "Allow" to grant CloudTrail permissions to write to the log group.

custom.whenBody: When your source isn't in the catalog. Forward arbitrary syslog or JSON to UTMStack and define a parser to normalize fields.
custom.parserBody: UTMStack will auto-detect JSON keys and propose field mappings. You can override mappings in the parser editor and add Grok patterns for free-form text.

socAi.title: SOC-AI Configuration
socAi.subtitle: Configure the AI agent that triages alerts and powers the operations assistant.

provider.label: Provider
provider.hint: Selects the wire format. Anything other than Anthropic uses the OpenAI-compatible API.

model.label: Model
model.hint: Model identifier exposed by the provider.

url.label: API URL
url.hint: Leave empty to use the provider's default endpoint.

apiKey.label: API key
apiKey.setHint: A key is stored. Leave blank to keep it.

authType.label: Auth type
authType.hint: How the API key is sent (bearer header, a custom header, or none).

authHeaderName.label: Auth header name
authHeaderName.hint: Header carrying the key (e.g. api-key for Azure).

customHeaders.label: Custom headers (JSON)
customHeaders.hint: Extra headers merged into every request. Values are encrypted; "*****" keeps the stored one.

maxToolIterations.label: Max tool iterations
maxToolIterations.hint: Cap on the agent's plan -> tool -> observe loop.

autoAnalyze.label: Auto-analyze alerts
autoAnalyze.hint: Triage incoming alerts in real time.

changeAlertStatus.label: Change alert status
changeAlertStatus.hint: Let the agent set an alert's status during triage.

automaticIncidentCreation.label: Create incidents
automaticIncidentCreation.hint: Let the agent open incidents from triaged alerts.

allowedWriteTools.label: Allowed write tools
allowedWriteTools.hint: One MCP tool name per line the triage agent may use (e.g. alerts.update_status). Notes are always allowed.

socAi.invalidHeaders: Custom headers must be a valid JSON object

applyTags.label: Apply tags
applyTags.hint: Let the agent tag alerts during triage.

socAi.capsCaption: Read access is always on. Choose what the agent may change — during triage and in chat. Anything left off, the agent will decline and point the user back here.

note.azure: Paste your full Azure deployment endpoint as the URL; the model is your deployment name. Auth uses the api-key header.
note.ollama: Point the URL at your Ollama host. No API key is needed for a local instance.
note.custom: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Set the URL, auth and any extra headers your gateway needs.

alerts.hint: Change status, apply tags, add notes, manage tag rules.

datasources.hint: Edit data source groups and labels.
